pinpoint: Witt Letter as quoted at SRC-021 P22
what_it_establishes: That Shellpoint, in writing on 2026-01-16, told Plaintiffs that MEB Loan Trust VIII is the current owner of the loan.
what_it_does_not_establish: That MEB owns the debt. A servicer's letter is a statement by the servicer about its own record, not proof of ownership. It does not identify the instrument by which MEB acquired the debt, and it does not address the note.
gap: No purchase agreement, trust schedule, or investor record connecting MEB to this loan is among the sources.
notes: Most useful as a party statement to be set against TRF-004, not as proof of ownership.

what_it_establishes: That an instrument assigning the Security Deed to MEB was recorded on 2024-02-19 in Deed Book 11187, Page 717, and what that instrument recites.
what_it_does_not_establish: That the underlying transfer occurred, was authorised, or conveyed the NOTE. Recording establishes recording. In Georgia the security follows the debt, so an assignment of the deed alone does not establish a right to enforce the obligation.
gap: The note, any endorsement or allonge, and evidence of who holds the original are all absent from the sources.
supporting_authority: UNRESEARCHED - whether Plaintiffs may challenge this assignment at all turns on Ames v. JP Morgan Chase Bank, 298 Ga. 732 (2016), which has NOT been read in this matter.
notes: THE INSTRUMENT ITSELF WAS NOT READ. Every conclusion here rests on SRC-021's quotation of it.

what_it_establishes: That Shellpoint took this loan onto its servicing system on 2024-07-07 with an opening principal of $140,288.02 and a late-charge balance of $624.00.
what_it_does_not_establish: The source or scope of Shellpoint's authority to service, or for whom. Boarding a loan is an operational act; the servicing agreement is what confers authority.
gap: No servicing agreement, power of attorney, or transfer notice is among the sources.
notes: Servicing authority is rarely contested and is not contested here.

what_it_establishes: Shellpoint's own written statement that it is a debt collector attempting to collect a debt.
what_it_does_not_establish: Its status under 15 U.S.C. 1692a(6), which turns on the statutory definition and on whether the debt was in default when acquired. A self-description is strong evidence of that status and is not conclusive of it.
gap: Nothing - the supporting fact (default status at acquisition) is itself documented at SRC-013 row 07/07/24 read with SRC-012's 'due for January 1, 2024'.
supporting_authority: UNRESEARCHED - SRC-021 P25 cites Davidson v. Capital One Bank (USA), N.A., 797 F.3d 1309 (11th Cir. 2015), which has NOT been verified in this matter.
notes: ONE OF THE BEST-SUPPORTED PROPOSITIONS IN THE MATTER: a party admission plus the defendant's own boarding record plus its own default reckoning.

what_it_establishes: That as of 2026-03-24 the registry's investor field for this MIN read FREED Mortgage Trust 2022-HE1.
what_it_does_not_establish: That FREED owns the debt, holds the note, or may enforce anything. A registry field is populated by the servicer, answers 'investor' rather than 'owner', and is frequently stale. The lookup itself was not seen.
gap: No trust document, schedule, or investor report connecting this loan to FREED.
notes: Its value is as evidence that the defendants' records are inconsistent, not as proof that FREED owns anything.

what_it_establishes: That MERS was designated nominee for the lender and its successors and grantee of record under the Security Deed.
what_it_does_not_establish: Any beneficial interest. A nominee holds legal title for another and has no economic stake; the designation is not a claim to own or enforce the debt.
notes: MERS is a defendant here but asserts no right against Plaintiffs on this record.
